# Reader ergonomics

> How to write notes, documents and files that cost the reader least, by what cognitive science, psycholinguistics and software engineering have measured. Every principle carries its grade of evidence.

Each page's markdown source is served at the same path with a .md extension.

## Standard

- [Standard](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/standard.md): the one-page card to follow, with every principle and its grade
- [Contributing](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/AGENTS.md): rules for changing this repository
- [Extending](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/extending.md): what an extension of this standard can rely on

## Collection: files and folders

- [Browsable folders](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/collection/browsable-folders.md): a collection is shallow and broad: two levels rather than three, and folders a reader can scan, of at least 3 and at most about 32 entries.
- [Dependencies without cycles](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/collection/dependencies-without-cycles.md): code dependencies between folders never form a cycle, so every folder sits on a level above everything it uses.
- [Group by what changes together](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/collection/group-by-what-changes-together.md): a folder holds what serves one purpose and changes together, not files of one type; other ways of grouping are carried by links and indexes.
- [Names predict content](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/collection/names-predict-content.md): a reader can predict what a file, folder or heading holds from its name before opening it, and each thing has one name throughout.
- [One place per fact](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/collection/one-place-per-fact.md): each piece of knowledge that must change together lives in one file; every other place links to it.
- [One role per file](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/collection/one-role-per-file.md): a file holds one role: what it does fits one sentence, and its parts change for the same reasons.
- [Portable paths](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/collection/portable-paths.md): every path in a repository can be checked out on any common filesystem.
- [Size is a prompt](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/collection/size-is-a-prompt.md): past a length, a file is asked to state its role; size alone never decides a split.
- [Tunables in config](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/collection/tunables-in-config.md): a value someone will set (a quota, a threshold, a price) lives in a configuration file, read at run time, and a value nobody has measured yet is tagged PROVISIONAL.

## Document: order and depth

- [Define before use](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/document/define-before-use.md): every term and symbol is defined at or before its first use, premises come in the order they are needed, and each thing keeps one name.
- [One mode per document](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/document/one-mode-per-document.md): each document serves one mode of reading (learning by doing, doing a task, looking something up, or understanding why) and says which.
- [Overview first](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/document/overview-first.md): a document opens with what it is about and how it is organised (its parts, in a few lines or a simple map) before any detail.
- [Retrieval prompts](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/document/retrieval-prompts.md): a document meant to be learned ends each part with a few questions the reader answers from memory, with the answers folded, and is reread after a gap.
- [Shallow outline](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/document/shallow-outline.md): what matters most sits at the top of a document's hierarchy, and the outline stays shallow: at most three levels of headings.
- [Short reference distance](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/document/short-reference-distance.md): each concept sits close to the places that use it, and the order of a document is chosen so that prerequisites come first and the total distance between definitions and uses is small.
- [Worked examples with subgoals](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/document/worked-examples-with-subgoals.md): a method is taught by a solved example whose steps are named by what they achieve, then faded: the next examples leave more steps to the reader.

## Sentence: density, locality and nesting

- [Even information density](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/sentence/even-information-density.md): a text says no more than the reader needs, and spreads what it says: no sentence packs several new ideas, and a dense term arrives after its context.
- [Given before new](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/sentence/given-before-new.md): a sentence starts from what the reader already has (the topic, or what the previous sentence ended on) and ends on what is new.
- [Shallow nesting](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/sentence/shallow-nesting.md): a sentence puts at most one clause inside another; with two nested clauses, readers already misread.
- [Short dependencies](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/sentence/short-dependencies.md): words that depend on each other stay close: a subject near its verb, a modifier next to what it modifies, a pronoun near what it refers to.

## Page: figures, layout and type

- [Draw relations](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/page/draw-relations.md): a relation, a set, a quantity or a process is shown as a figure placed with the words that explain it, not as words alone.
- [Figure next to its text](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/page/figure-next-to-its-text.md): the words that explain a figure, a formula or a block of code sit beside or inside it: not on another page, not below the fold.
- [Readable measure](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/page/readable-measure.md): body text has a line length of about 45 to 75 characters, a size in the fluent range, and line spacing of at least 1.5.
- [Signal the structure](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/page/signal-the-structure.md): the structure of a text is visible before it is read: headings that name their content, lists for parallel items, tables for comparisons, bold for the defined term.
- [Sufficient contrast](https://tewf.github.io/reader-ergonomics/principles/page/sufficient-contrast.md): text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background, dark text on a light ground by default, with a dark theme offered and never forced.
